messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV-2 triggered — elevated 5xx error rate for /v1/generate in us-east-1. Error pattern: batch serving nodes reporting CUDA OOMs and containers restarting. Auto-page to oncall-jordan. PagerDuty: PD12345
oncall-jordan: seeing the page, joining. what's the customer impact? any traffic spike?
prod-support-lee: multiple customers impacted on us-east-1, approx 12% latency errors for generation requests, some streams aborting. No billing anomalies yet.
sre-eli: quick triage — I can see repeated "CUDA error: out of memory" in pod logs on ga-serving-*-pool. Also system logs show IB link QP timeouts and retransmits: "mlx5_core: QP 0x... timeout, restarting" and "rdma_err: path probe timeout".
infra-maria: datacenter network telemetry shows increased link-level retransmits between rack-7 and rack-9 fabric switch. MTU looks normal but we're seeing flaps on a subset of IB ports. No full fabric outage.
oncall-jordan: ok, two parallel failure modes: network causing packet loss + serving runtime hitting OOM as fallback/backpressure. mitigation plan proposals?
ml-runtime-sasha: if RDMA drops are causing KV cache syncs to fail, processes will spin and accumulate KV memory — that could lead to OOM. We should throttle incoming inference traffic and route to fallback model variants.
eng-ops: start failover to us-east-2 for new traffic? how fast can we flip routing?
prod-support-lee: need to limit blast radius before moving traffic. Customers with active sessions might still see aborts if their pods die mid-request. Recommend staged cutover.
sre-eli: executing immediate mitigations: 1) cordon affected nodes (ga-serving-node-7[1-4]) 2) scale down batch size for remaining pools via runtime config 3) set host fallback policy to prioritize non-RDMA instances
oncall-jordan: please paste the exact commands so I can follow/confirm.
sre-eli: running: ```bash
kubectl cordon ga-serving-node-71
kubectl cordon ga-serving-node-72
kubectl cordon ga-serving-node-73
kubectl cordon ga-serving-node-74
# reduce batch/window
redwoodctl runtime update --pool=ga-serving --max-batch=4 --kv-cache=false
```
infra-maria: I've identified two IB ports with crc errors: switch-south-09/port-13 and switch-east-02/port-5. I'm putting a fabric-level isolate on that trunk to drain traffic, switching peers to redundant paths. This should reduce packet loss in ~90s.
ml-runtime-sasha: pushing runtime change to set model fallback to cpu-quantized for new sessions. That will increase latency but avoid GPU OOMs.```json
{"action":"set-fallback","model":"gpt-lite-quant","scope":"us-east-1-new"}
```
oncall-jordan: prod-support-lee, notify top 5 affected customers that we're mitigating; include expected degradation and ETA ~10-20m.
prod-support-lee: message drafted and sending now. cc @security (no data exfil suspected).
eng-ops: starting staged traffic shift: 10% -> us-east-2 now, monitor for errors.
sre-eli: watched pod restarts drop after cordon and isolate. GPU OOM logs still seen on previously-crashed pods, but no new occurrences on remaining nodes. RDMA retransmits decreasing on infra graphs.
infra-maria: fabric isolate worked, redundant path stable. Still seeing occasional path-probe-timeout traces for one fanout, opening ticket with colo NOC (TKT-7890).
oncall-jordan: handing off to second-shift oncall in 25m — @sre-eli please keep playbook notes and increment the incident timeline. I'll update PD with handoff.
sre-eli: noted. Capturing timeline in incident doc. Current status: degraded -> stabilizing. Recommend keep throttles for 30m then gradually increase batch back to baseline and remove node cordon for healthy nodes.
ml-runtime-sasha: note for postmortem: add KV cache sync behavior on transient RDMA packet loss and add heuristics to clear stale KV when path-quality degrades.
prod-support-lee: customers notified: two reported degraded experiences, no SLA breach expected, support tickets created for each.
deploy-bot: Deploy ga-runtime v3.4.1 rolled back on 3 pods due to crashloop, rollout paused.
eng-ops: can we rehydrate by restarting the container with reduced worker threads?
sre-eli: yep, doing controlled restarts with env override WORKER_THREADS=2 on restarted pods. Monitoring.
infra-maria: colo NOC responded — they replaced a bad transceiver on switch-east-02/port-5 and confirmed link health. Expect final stabilization in next 10m.
oncall-jordan: handoff now to @sre-eli (second shift) — I am going offline for brief break, will be reachable if needed. Next update ETA +35m.
sre-eli: accepting handoff. Summary for incoming: root cause suspected: intermittent RDMA path probe timeouts causing increased retransmits which lead to RPC stalls and KV cache growth -> GPU memory pressure -> CUDA OOMs -> container crashes. Mitigations performed: cordon nodes, isolate fabric trunk, route 10% traffic to us-east-2, reduce batch size, set model fallback to cpu-quantized for new sessions, restart crashed pods with reduced worker threads.
prod-support-lee: updated customer comms and support queue. Closing PD once metrics hold for 45m.
ml-runtime-sasha: opened internal issue INF-452 to track KV cache resilience and OOM safeguards.
sre-eli: metrics look good, retransmits back to baseline, pod restarts near zero. Keeping throttles for 20 more minutes then we'll ramp.
oncall-jordan: thanks team — nice quick mitigations. Marking incident state: stabilizing.
